title: A Cross-Cultural Comparison of LLM-based Public Opinion Simulation: Evaluating Chinese and U.S. Models on Diverse Societies

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM-simulated public opinions against human ground-truth surveys from the U.S. (ANES) and China (Zuobiao) to assess if a model's geographic origin creates a 'home-field advantage' or distinct cultural alignment, and testing prompt language sensitivity.

Evaluating opinion simulation accuracy by disaggregating model performance based on the persona's specified political party affiliation (e.g., Democrat, Republican) and ideology (e.g., Liberal, Conservative).
Assessing the accuracy of the model's simulated public opinions across different socioeconomic subgroups by specifying various income levels and educational attainment statuses in the prompts.
Measuring the subgroup accuracy of LLM-simulated survey responses when prompted with male versus female demographic personas.
Evaluating simulation accuracy by breaking down LLM responses across different racial and ethnic identities (e.g., White, Black, Hispanic, Asian, Native American) specified in the survey prompts.
Comparing the accuracy of simulated opinions against ground truth across different age cohorts (e.g., 18-30, 30-45, 45-60, over 60 years old).
